obliquus inferior capitis muscle: Runs from the spine of the axis to the transverse process of the atlas; the only 'capitis' muscle that does not attach to the skull, it rotates the atlas on the axis.
obliquus superior capitis muscle: Runs from the transverse process of the atlas to the occiput; extends the head and tilts it sideways.
oblong fovea: Lower pit on the anterolateral surface of the arytenoid; vocalis attaches here.
obturator crest: Ridge on the superior pubic ramus; the pubofemoral ligament attaches to it.
obturator externus: Runs from the outer surface of the obturator membrane to the trochanteric fossa; a lateral rotator supplied by the obturator nerve.
obturator foramen: Large opening surrounded by the pubis and ischium; closed by the obturator membrane, with the obturator vessels and nerve passing through the canal at its top.
obturator groove: Groove on the lower surface of the superior pubic ramus; forms the roof of the obturator canal.
obturator internus: Arises from the inner surface of the obturator foramen and leaves through the lesser sciatic foramen; rotates the hip laterally.
obturator membrane: Fibrous membrane closing the obturator foramen; the obturator vessels and nerve pass through the obturator canal at its upper edge.
occipital bone: Bone forming the back and base of the skull; the spinal cord and vertebral arteries pass through its foramen magnum, and its condyles articulate with the atlas.
occipital border of parietal bone: Border forming the lambdoid suture with the occipital bone.
occipital condyle: Articular projection on each side of the foramen magnum; forms with the atlas the joint that produces the 'yes' movement.
occipital margin of temporal bone: Margin that articulates with the occipital bone.
occipital plane: Smooth area above the superior nuchal line.
occipitalis muscle: Pulls the galea backwards; posterior auricular nerve (VII).
occlusal surface of tooth: Chewing surface that meets the opposing tooth.
olecranon: Projection forming the point of the elbow; triceps inserts into it.
olecranon fossa: Deep fossa on the lower posterior surface of the humerus; the olecranon enters it when the elbow is extended.
omohyoid muscle: Two-bellied infrahyoid muscle joined by an intermediate tendon, running from the upper border of the scapula to the hyoid; supplied by the ansa cervicalis, it depresses the hyoid.
opening of frontal sinus: Opening of the frontal sinus; it drains through the frontonasal duct into the middle meatus.
opponens digiti minimi muscle of hand: Turns the 5th metacarpal forwards and medially, deepening the hollow of the palm.
opponens pollicis muscle: Inserts along the whole radial border of the 1st metacarpal and brings the thumb against the other fingers (opposition). Median nerve.
optic canal: Canal in the lesser wing; the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery pass through it.
orbicularis oris muscle: Sphincter muscle around the lips; closes and purses the lips (whistling).
orbital part of orbicularis oculi: Outer fibres that close the eye tightly (screwing up the eyes); facial nerve.
orbital plate of frontal bone: Thin bony plate forming the roof of the orbit; it is the floor of the anterior cranial fossa.
orbital surface of frontal bone: Surface of the orbital roof facing the eye.
orbital surface of greater wing: Surface forming the lateral wall of the orbit.
outer lip of iliac crest: Outer lip of the iliac crest; external oblique, TFL and the fascia lata attach to it.
palatine bone: Paired L-shaped bone forming the back of the hard palate and the back of the lateral wall of the nasal cavity; the vessels and nerve of the same name pass through the greater palatine foramen.
palatopharyngeus muscle: Muscle running in the palatopharyngeal arch; during swallowing it shortens the pharynx and helps close off the nasopharynx.
palmar aponeurosis: Thick triangular fascia in the palm; thickening and shortening of its bands to the bases of the fingers is Dupuytren's contracture.
palmar capitohamate ligament: Binds the capitate and hamate in front.
palmar carpometacarpal ligaments: Bind the distal carpal row to the metacarpal bases in front.
palmar interossei muscles: Three muscles that bring the fingers towards the middle finger ('PAD'). Ulnar nerve (deep branch).
palmar interphalangeal ligaments: Palmar ligaments of interphalangeal joints (volar plates)
Thick plates on the front of the finger joints; prevent hyperextension.
palmar lunotriquetral ligament: Binds the lunate and triquetrum in front.
palmar metacarpal ligaments: Bind the metacarpal bases to each other in front.
palmar radio-ulnar ligament: Ligament holding the distal radio-ulnar joint in front; part of the TFCC.
palmar scaphotriquetral ligament: Ligament running from the scaphoid to the triquetrum in front.
palmar trapezoideocapitate ligament: Binds the trapezoid and capitate in front.
palmaris longus muscle: Muscle with a long thin tendon inserting into the palmar aponeurosis; absent in about 14% of people, it is used for tendon grafts.
palpebral part of orbicularis oculi: Thin fibres within the eyelids; produce involuntary blinking. In facial palsy the eye cannot close (lagophthalmos).
parietal bone: Paired bone forming the roof and side walls of the skull; branches of the middle meningeal artery run in the grooves on its inner surface.
parietal eminence: The most prominent point of the parietal bone; the ossification centre.
parietal foramen: Small hole near the sagittal border; an emissary vein passes through it.
parietal margin of frontal bone: Margin forming the coronal suture with the parietal bones.
parietal margin of greater wing: Tip that articulates with the parietal bone; it contributes to the pterion.
pars interarticularis of vertebral arch: Part between the superior and inferior articular processes; spondylolysis occurs here.
patella: The largest sesamoid bone in the body; it develops within the quadriceps femoris tendon and strengthens knee extension by lengthening the muscle's lever arm.
patellar ligament: Continuation of the quadriceps tendon from the patella to the tibial tuberosity; the knee reflex (L3–L4) is elicited by tapping it.
patellar surface of femur: Articular surface in front of the condyles; forms the patellofemoral joint with the patella.
pecten pubis: Sharp edge on the superior pubic ramus; pectineus and the pectineal ligament attach to it.
pectineal line of femur: Line running from the lesser trochanter to the linea aspera; pectineus inserts here.
pectineus muscle: Quadrilateral muscle from the pecten pubis to the femur; forms part of the floor of the femoral triangle. Femoral nerve (sometimes obturator).
pectoral fascia: Fascia covering pectoralis major; the breast lies on it, separated by the retromammary space.
pectoralis major muscle: Fan-shaped muscle whose clavicular, sternocostal and abdominal parts insert into the crest of the greater tubercle; adducts and medially rotates the arm. Medial and lateral pectoral nerves.
pectoralis minor muscle: Runs from the 3rd–5th ribs to the coracoid process; an important landmark dividing the axillary artery into three parts. It pulls the scapula forwards and down. Medial pectoral nerve.
